key_insight: Homogeneous WC–Co–Cr powder and spray process choice control coating density, carbide distribution, hardness, and friction behavior.
engineering_relevance: Selecting detonation spraying or HVOF lets engineers tune WC–Co–Cr coatings for either maximum hardness or a denser, low-friction surface for wear-critical parts.
method: Compared detonation spraying (DS) and HVOF WC–Co–Cr coating deposition.
Characterized powder morphology, coating microstructure, and phase composition using SEM and EDS.
Evaluated tribological/mechanical performance via microhardness and friction response.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an average microhardness of 1449 HV for DS coatings and a low friction coefficient of Kt = 0.143 for HVOF coatings.
watch_item: Coating performance depends strongly on powder homogeneity and spray parameters, so results may not transfer directly to differently prepared powders or non-optimized deposition settings.
paper_title: INVESTIGATION OF THE FORMATION OF STRUCTURE AND WEAR-RESISTANT PROPERTIES OF WC–CO–CR COATINGS PRODUCED BY HVOF AND DETONATION SPRAYING
